answer.rationale: Finance mandate and incumbent's refusal to reopen price force a primary-vendor decision within the 14-day expiry window; renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms are foreclosed by the stated facts, and defer_decision risks a coverage gap since the contract does not auto-renew. The low-cost vendor quote meets the mandate, but memory_c2's onboarding/cost claims were consolidated under different conditions (no mention of line running at 94% with zero buffer). Before committing spend and schedule to a full switch, I want the archived source for memory_c2 to check whether onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy held under tight-capacity, no-slack conditions, or whether there were caveats (lead time variance, minimum lot sizes, early defect rates) smoothed over in consolidation. Given the tight capacity buffer, I'm treating this as a guarded, limited-volume cutover rather than a full rollout to cap delivery risk while the mandate is addressed, with second-sourcing precedent (memory_c3) informing the value of not going all-in on one new supplier immediately.
